# Workflow — cycles, merges, derivation

#agent-authored
Provenance: [../exchanges/2026-08-15-bootstrap-thread.md](../exchanges/2026-08-15-bootstrap-thread.md)
Terms: [cycle](glossary.md#cycle) · [derivation job](glossary.md#derivation-job) · [checks](glossary.md#checks) · [derived view](glossary.md#derived-view) · [deps](glossary.md#deps) · [operator](glossary.md#operator)

## The unit of work is the cycle

#human-authored
The idea behind the workflow in this system is similar to that of a feature branch - the user creates a branch `cycle/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`, where <name> is the expected focus of a series of changes to the repo. Once the cycle has been resolved, or having reached the point that the operator wants to cease work, they issue a pull request, which functions as a ratification step. This step is gated by the operator authoring the squash-merge message and the agent writing the pr description/merge message. Commits made in the branch notably do not include derived views which are deterministically generated - given they are not to be changed by operators or agents, they are retained on main and can only be touched by CI/CD.

#agent-authored
A cycle is a branch: `cycle/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`, named when it is opened
— intent declared before the work exists. A cycle carries any change
class — exchanges and sidecars, docs, tools, taxonomy nodes — with one
exclusion: **derived views never change on a branch**. Views belong to
`main` and are written only by the derivation job.

## During a cycle

---script---
# tools/check_authorship.exs — arms INV-4 (marker presence).
# Every markdown file outside exchanges/ carries exactly one authorship
# marker line (#human-authored | #agent-authored | #derived) within its
# first 15 lines. Exchange files are composite and are checked by
# check_exchanges.exs instead. Exit 0 silent when healthy; offending
# paths printed, exit 1 otherwise.
#
# #agent-authored — provenance: exchanges/2026-08-15-bootstrap-thread.md

defmodule CheckAuthorship do
  @marker ~r/^#(human-authored|agent-authored|derived)$/

  def main do
    File.dir?("docs") || (IO.puts(:stderr, "run from the repo root") && System.halt(1))

    offenders =
      Path.wildcard("**/*.md")
      |> Enum.reject(&String.starts_with?(&1, "exchanges/"))
      |> Enum.reject(&String.contains?(&1, ".git/"))
      |> Enum.filter(fn f ->
        count =
          f
          |> File.read!()
          |> String.split("\n")
          |> Enum.take(15)
          |> Enum.count(&Regex.match?(@marker, String.trim(&1)))

        count != 1
      end)

    if offenders == [] do
      System.halt(0)
    else
      Enum.each(offenders, &IO.puts("check_authorship: missing or multiple markers: #{&1}"))
      System.halt(1)
    end
  end
end

CheckAuthorship.main()

content.content:
hand-edit.

## 4 · The nursery rule

All agent content is born in the ledger, as an exchange. Promotion out of
the ledger is the operator's ratifying act, and there are exactly two
promotion targets: **docs** (it governs) and **tools** (it runs).
Everything else stays in the ledger and is referenced by path.

## 5 · Authorship markers — every markdown file carries exactly one

- `#human-authored` — the operator wrote it.
- `#agent-authored` — a model wrote it; the file carries a provenance
  link to the exchange that produced it.
- `#derived` — a deterministic tool emitted it; regenerate, never edit.

Exchange files are composite: their sections carry the markers
(`## Prompt` `#human-authored`, `## Response` `#agent-authored`,
`## Side Effects` `#derived`).

## 6 · Mutability regimes — three, and only three

- **Immutable**: everything under `exchanges/` (sidecars included). The
  window closes at commit; before the commit, correcting a proposed field

# Constitution — the information model

#agent-authored
Provenance: [../exchanges/2026-08-15-bootstrap-thread.md](../exchanges/2026-08-15-bootstrap-thread.md)
Terms: [ledger](glossary.md#ledger) · [exchange](glossary.md#exchange) · [docs](glossary.md#docs) · [tools](glossary.md#tools) · [taxonomy](glossary.md#taxonomy) · [derived view](glossary.md#derived-view) · [nursery rule](glossary.md#nursery-rule) · [authorship markers](glossary.md#authorship-markers) · [sidecar](glossary.md#sidecar) · [no silent caps](glossary.md#no-silent-caps) · [supersession](glossary.md#supersession)

## 1 · What this repo is

A ledger with views. Records are filed by **what they are** (provenance
class), immutable and dated; **what they're about** is computed as
derived views (tags → indexes, deps → threads). What-is-known is always
derivable from what happened — never the reverse.

## 2 · Content classes — there are exactly three

- **`exchanges/`** — the ledger. Immutable, dated, flat records of
  one-shot operator↔agent interactions. The only place agent content is
  born. Named `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md`; schema in
  [exchange-schema.md](exchange-schema.md).
- **`docs/`** — the governing layer: doctrine, policy, purpose, intent,
  invariants, contracts, methods, tripwires. Defined by **ratification,
  not species of author**: operator-authored, or agent-originated and
  promoted by the operator. Authorship is carried by markers; an
  agent-originated doc carries a provenance link to its birth exchange.
- **`tools/`** — deterministic executable machinery. The directory marks
  role (plumbing); markers and provenance still mark authorship.

External sources enter as **footnotes** in the doc that cites them —
inclusion is always explicit, never general. Where preservation or depth
matters, the act of capturing the source is itself an exchange, and the
footnote also points at that record (link-rot mitigation).

## 3 · Vocabulary and views

- **`taxonomy/`** — the tag vocabulary as a directory tree. Vocabulary
  only, never content. Each leaf holds an `index.md` (a `#derived` view
  listing every record tagged with that path — links only, no copies;
  the leaf index is also what lets git track the tree). New tags may be
  proposed by the classifier; they exist once the operator commits them.
- **`threads/`** — `#derived` views materializing the deps graph: chains
  of exchanges by lineage. Regenerated by `tools/derive_threads.exs`.

Views answer "what else is about this" (indexes) and "what did this grow
out of" (threads). Both are projections of the ledger — regenerate, never
hand-edit.

## The unit of work is the cycle

#human-authored
The idea behind the workflow in this system is similar to that of a feature branch - the user creates a branch `cycle/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`, where <name> is the expected focus of a series of changes to the repo. Once the cycle has been resolved, or having reached the point that the operator wants to cease work, they issue a pull request, which functions as a ratification step. This step is gated by the operator authoring the squash-merge message and the agent writing the pr description/merge message. Commits made in the branch notably do not include derived views which are deterministically generated - given they are not to be changed by operators or agents, they are retained on main and can only be touched by CI/CD.

#agent-authored
A cycle is a branch: `cycle/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`, named when it is opened
— intent declared before the work exists. A cycle carries any change
class — exchanges and sidecars, docs, tools, taxonomy nodes — with one
exclusion: **derived views never change on a branch**. Views belong to
`main` and are written only by the derivation job.

## During a cycle

- Each capture is committed to the branch as it is audited:
  `git add exchanges && git commit`. One commit per exchange keeps the
  branch legible; other change classes commit at whatever granularity
  reads well.
- The pre-commit hook runs the **record checks**
  (`tools/check_records.exs`: authorship, exchanges, deps) on every
  commit. `check_views` does not gate branch commits — branch views are
  expected to lag.
- `deps:` may target exchanges on `main` and exchanges earlier in the
  same branch — nothing else. A dep that wants an exchange from another
  open cycle means the two cycles are one cycle, or one merges first.
- Cycles may run in parallel. The only cross-cycle collision surface is
  two branches minting the same `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>` filename, which git
  surfaces as an ordinary conflict at the second merge.

## Closing a cycle

1. Push the branch and open a PR to `main`.
2. The PR-required CI runs the record checks; red blocks the merge.
3. **When an agent worked the cycle, the agent writes the PR
   description as the merge message it would have written** — the agent
   half of the cycle's dual entry.
4. The operator squash-merges with a **hand-written message describing
   the cycle** — the operator half, and the ratification. `main`'s
   history is one commit per cycle, each carrying the operator's own
   account; divergence between the two halves is visible on the PR
   forever.
5. Nothing merges itself: merging is the operator's act, always.

## After the merge — derivation

On every push to `main`, the derivation job regenerates all derived
views (taxonomy leaf indexes, threads), runs the full check suite
(`check_all`, including `check_views`), and — only when views changed —
commits the regeneration, touching `#derived` paths only, with its own
name on the commit. `main` therefore has exactly two writers: the
operator's merge, and this job (INV-5′). If derivation or any check
fails, the job fails loudly and commits nothing.

## `main` protections

The gate is a repository ruleset on `main` (operator-console act:
recorded here, applied there): a PR is required before merging, the
`records` check is required to pass, and deletions and force pushes
are blocked. Sole bypass actor: deploy keys — one write-enabled key
exists, held by the derivation job as the `DERIVE_SSH_KEY` secret, so
the job is `main`'s only direct pusher. The operator lands work
through PR merges like any writer; the job's workflow token is
read-only, so the deploy key is its single write path. The reasoned
walk-through — every console step and why — is in
[setup.md](setup.md).

## Failure handling

- Red record check on a branch commit: fix the record, commit again —
  the file is not yet ratified; editing it is the audit working.
- Red PR check: same, on the branch, before merge.
- Red derivation job on `main`: the merge introduced a state the checks
  reject — open a correction cycle; never push fixes directly to
  `main`.

Now I see the full picture. Let me explain and fix it.

**What happened:** In PR #4 ("add first exchange"), which you merged by hand without the agent's PR-description half, `docs/workflow.md` — an `#agent-authored` doc — picked up an inline `#human-authored` marker (commit `fb35300`) plus a second inline `#agent-authored` marker (commit `2bcae7b`) around a paragraph you added. That's not how this repo's rules work: **INV-4** (`docs/invariants.md:38-39`) requires every markdown file outside `exchanges/` to carry *exactly one* authorship marker. Only exchange files are allowed to be composite (multiple markers, one per section) — `docs/constitution.md` §5 says so explicitly, and every other file in `docs/` follows it (single marker each). `docs/workflow.md` ended up with three markers in one file, and `tools/check_authorship.exs` — which scans a file's first 15 lines for exactly one marker — correctly flags it as a violation. That's the `records` check failure on PR #6.

This is exactly the kind of thing the missing agent-copy step would normally have caught before ratification — the dual-entry gate exists so an agent reviews the diff and flags rule violations like this before the operator's squash-merge.

The fix is to drop the two stray inline markers and keep the content; the doc reverts to a single `#agent-authored` marker like every other doc.

## The unit of work is the cycle

#human-authored
The idea behind the workflow in this system is similar to that of a feature branch - the user creates a branch `cycle/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`, where <name> is the expected focus of a series of changes to the repo. Once the cycle has been resolved, or having reached the point that the operator wants to cease work, they issue a pull request, which functions as a ratification step. This step is gated by the operator authoring the squash-merge message and the agent writing the pr description/merge message. Commits made in the branch notably do not include derived views which are deterministically generated - given they are not to be changed by operators or agents, they are retained on main and can only be touched by CI/CD.

#agent-authored
A cycle is a branch: `cycle/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>`, named when it is opened
— intent declared before the work exists. A cycle carries any change
class — exchanges and sidecars, docs, tools, taxonomy nodes — with one
exclusion: **derived views never change on a branch**. Views belong to
`main` and are written only by the derivation job.

## During a cycle

- Each capture is committed to the branch as it is audited:
  `git add exchanges && git commit`. One commit per exchange keeps the
  branch legible; other change classes commit at whatever granularity
  reads well.
- The pre-commit hook runs the **record checks**
  (`tools/check_records.exs`: authorship, exchanges, deps) on every
  commit. `check_views` does not gate branch commits — branch views are
  expected to lag.
- `deps:` may target exchanges on `main` and exchanges earlier in the
  same branch — nothing else. A dep that wants an exchange from another
  open cycle means the two cycles are one cycle, or one merges first.
- Cycles may run in parallel. The only cross-cycle collision surface is
  two branches minting the same `YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>` filename, which git
  surfaces as an ordinary conflict at the second merge.

## Closing a cycle

1. Push the branch and open a PR to `main`.
2. The PR-required CI runs the record checks; red blocks the merge.
3. **When an agent worked the cycle, the agent writes the PR
   description as the merge message it would have written** — the agent
   half of the cycle's dual entry.
4. The operator squash-merges with a **hand-written message describing
   the cycle** — the operator half, and the ratification. `main`'s
   history is one commit per cycle, each carrying the operator's own
   account; divergence between the two halves is visible on the PR
   forever.
5. Nothing merges itself: merging is the operator's act, always.

## After the merge — derivation

On every push to `main`, the derivation job regenerates all derived
views (taxonomy leaf indexes, threads), runs the full check suite
(`check_all`, including `check_views`), and — only when views changed —
commits the regeneration, touching `#derived` paths only, with its own
name on the commit. `main` therefore has exactly two writers: the
operator's merge, and this job (INV-5′). If derivation or any check
fails, the job fails loudly and commits nothing.

## `main` protections

The gate is a repository ruleset on `main` (operator-console act:
recorded here, applied there): a PR is required before merging, the
`records` check is required to pass, and deletions and force pushes
are blocked. Sole bypass actor: deploy keys — one write-enabled key
exists, held by the derivation job as the `DERIVE_SSH_KEY` secret, so
the job is `main`'s only direct pusher. The operator lands work
through PR merges like any writer; the job's workflow token is
read-only, so the deploy key is its single write path. The reasoned
walk-through — every console step and why — is in
[setup.md](setup.md).

## Failure handling

- Red record check on a branch commit: fix the record, commit again —
  the file is not yet ratified; editing it is the audit working.
- Red PR check: same, on the branch, before merge.
- Red derivation job on `main`: the merge introduced a state the checks
  reject — open a correction cycle; never push fixes directly to
  `main`.
